page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton2 processor. Built on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture with Neoverse-N1 cores, this instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz with one thread per core. It features a cache hierarchy of 64 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core.

This instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. It delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The inclusion of local NVMe SSDs provides high-speed, low-latency local storage directly attached to the instance, which is beneficial for temporary data, caching, and scratch space.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48566.12 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11488.0. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 942.0 and a poor single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 7.26 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is strong for cached small blocks at 1894.65 GB/sec, but drops to 139.81 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. LLM inference performance is weak to poor, with text generation on a small 135M model reaching 26.11 tokens/sec.

Given its high memory density of 16 GB per core and integrated NVMe storage, the x2gd.8xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. It is well-suited for database operations, Redis caching layers, and memory-heavy enterprise applications. The instance is less suitable for compute-bound single-threaded tasks or large language model inference.
description: The Amazon Web Services x2gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server featuring 32 dedicated ARM64 cores powered by AWS Graviton2 (Neoverse-N1) processors running at 2.5 GHz. It is configured with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a high 16.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48566.12 and a Redis SET performance of 36.44 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 942.0. This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and caching layers, offering a resource-dense and cost-efficient configuration for applications requiring substantial memory capacity and local NVMe storage without demanding top-tier single-threaded CPU performance.
